intro: ARIES organizes its work in four research areas, implemented in phases. Two are active today and match the founding groups' expertise; two open as the center grows and colleagues from related fields join.

pillars.name: Deep Tech and Intelligent Systems
pillars.name_th: เทคโนโลยีขั้นสูงและระบบอัจฉริยะ
pillars.text: Structural inspection with artificial intelligence, digital twins, unmanned aerial vehicles and LiDAR; autonomous inspection pipelines; computer vision for classifying structural damage.
pillars.note: Current work: UAV-enhanced fatigue assessment of RC bridge girders; digital twin platform for network-level bridge management (NRCT 2026).

pillars.name: Structural Systems
pillars.name_th: ระบบโครงสร้างพื้นฐาน
pillars.text: Condition assessment and management of infrastructure systems from the component to the network level, covering bridges, buildings, dams and transport networks.
pillars.note: Current work: coastal concrete bridge damage detection and assessment (NRCT 2025, completed); field investigation of cracking in post-tensioned ledge girders.

pillars.name: Resilience and Multi-Hazard Assessment
pillars.name_th: ความต้านทานและการประเมินภัยพิบัติ
pillars.text: Integrated risk assessment and structural reliability covering earthquake, deterioration, corrosion and climate-change impacts, together with life-cycle management of structures.
pillars.note: Foundations: reliability updating of ageing RC structures with spatial corrosion; life-cycle reliability of deteriorating structures.

pillars.name: Advanced Materials and Durability
pillars.name_th: วัสดุขั้นสูงและความทนทาน
pillars.text: Advanced materials such as graphene quantum dots and ultra-high performance concrete, computational deterioration modelling, and low-carbon concrete.
pillars.note: Foundations: corrosion-product quantification by X-ray techniques; fiber-reinforced strengthening of concrete columns.

flagship.p1: Bridges are the proving ground for the first three years. The program builds a complete inspection-to-decision system: UAV and LiDAR survey, AI damage detection, a digital twin of each structure, condition assessment, and prioritization of maintenance across the whole network.
flagship.p2: What is different: prioritization at the network level rather than bridge by bridge; an engineer in the loop at every quality-control step; and data standards that owner agencies can adopt directly, so results move from research into practice.

steps.p: Image and point-cloud capture of the whole structure.
Computer vision classifies cracks, spalling and corrosion.
Geometry, damage and behaviour in one living model.
Structural evaluation with human-in-the-loop quality control.
Which bridge, which repair, in what order.
